Among the many Apple Intelligence features coming in iOS 27, the Passwords app will gain a particularly powerful capability: automatically changing your passwords for you.

The Passwords app in iOS 27, powered by Apple Intelligence, can fix your compromised login accounts on your behalf

The next generation of Apple Intelligence is at the heart of the upcoming iOS 27 and related software updates. One of the powerful new AI features relates to the Apple Passwords app.

Passwords launched two years ago as a dedicated management hub for login credentials, two-factor authentication codes, Wi-Fi passwords, passkeys, and more.

This app has always alerted you to problems with passwords in your database. For example, if your password has appeared in a data breach or is reused across multiple accounts, the Passwords app will notify you.

However, until now, you've still had to deal with these problematic login accounts manually.

But in iOS 27, Apple says that in many cases, new agentic AI features can change your passwords for you. According to its website:

With this feature, you can always keep your login accounts secure and use strong passwords without spending too much effort or time.

iOS 27 is currently in beta and is expected to be released to all users in a few weeks. The new Passwords feature is expected to debut in iOS 27.0, but availability in the beta has been unstable, so it may be pushed back to iOS 27.1 for its official release.

Have you used the new Passwords feature in the iOS 27 beta? How has your experience been? Feel free to share in the comments.
